title: Self-challenge of an overpriced position pays a reserve-funded reward and forgives the owner's debt (no bidder, loss minted via notifyLoss)
description: Discovery: Q4.5 / Q3.2 / ECON-02 (value derived from an owner-controlled parameter). The challenger reward (2% of volume) and the repayment are computed from volume = position.price * size, where price is set by the position owner. When no bidder averts the challenge, effectiveBid is 0 and hub calls zchf.notifyLoss(reward + repayment), which transfers from the equity reserve and mints the rest. The end() caller (anyone when there is no bidder) also receives the position's collateral. The owner (or a colluding second address) can therefore set a price slightly above market (nobody will pay price*size to avert), mint M ZCHF, then challenge and call end() himself: his own collateral comes back, his debt M is burned out of reserve/minted funds, and he collects a 2% reward on price*size.
root_cause: Reward and repayment are tied to the owner-chosen liquidation price rather than to the realised bid, and any shortfall versus the (possibly zero) bid is covered by notifyLoss (reserve, then fresh mint). There is no cap by market value and no protection against the owner being the challenger or the end() caller.

harm.who: FPS holders (equity reserve) and all ZCHF holders (dilution by minted loss cover)
harm.loses_what: reserve ZCHF equal to the owner's minted debt plus 2% of price*size per challenge, or newly minted unbacked ZCHF
harm.magnitude: up to position.minted plus 2% of price*collateral per self-challenge

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker opens (or clones) a position with price slightly above market and, after the init period, mints M ZCHF against collateral C.
2. A second attacker address calls launchChallenge(position, size) with its own collateral; no honest bidder bids because price*size exceeds market value.
3. After challengePeriod the attacker calls end(n): returnCollateral gives the challenger his own collateral back, recipient = msg.sender receives the position collateral C, effectiveBid = 0.

4. fundsNeeded = 2%*price*size + min(minted, price*size); hub calls zchf.notifyLoss(fundsNeeded), draining the equity reserve (then minting), pays the reward to the challenger and burns the repayment.
5. Result: attacker keeps M ZCHF and C and the reward; reserve/FPS holders absorb the loss.

preconditions.text: position price above market so nobody averts; governance did not veto in the init period (or the position is a clone, which has no veto window)

postconditions.text: equity reserve reduced / ZCHF supply inflated by the loss cover

rules_applied: R10:✓(worst state: large minted, no bids)
R12:✓(enablers: price raise, clone, no bidder)
depth_evidence: [BOUNDARY:bid=0 -> effectiveBid=0, fundsNeeded fully covered by reserve/mint]
postconditions_created: equity reserve reduced / ZCHF supply inflated by the loss cover

title: Owner can raise the liquidation price at any time (only a 3-day cooldown) and clones skip the veto window, allowing unbacked minting up to the limit
description: Discovery: Q3.1 / Q1.4 (sufficiency of the check). Governance's only protection against a bad price is the veto during the first 3 days (Position.deny, start check). adjustPrice() allows increasing the price without any collateral check or governance hook; it only triggers restrictMinting(3 days). A clone is created without veto window (cooldown storage starts at 0, no OPENING_FEE) and gets price = _mint*1e18/_coll, which is 0 for _mint = 0; the clone owner can then raise the price arbitrarily. After 3 days the owner mints up to the clone's limit against dust collateral.
root_cause: The price used by checkCollateral() is fully owner-controlled after the veto period, so the collateral invariant 'collateral * price >= minted' can be made trivially true; vetting by governance applies only at position creation, not to later price changes or clones.

harm.loses_what: backing of ZCHF minted against worthless collateral (up to the position/clone limit); loss falls on the reserve when the position is later liquidated
harm.magnitude: up to the limit given to the clone (half of the remaining limit of the original) or the original's limit

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker calls MintingHub.clonePosition(vettedPosition, minCollateral, 0): receives half of the remaining limit L, no veto window, price = 0.
2. Attacker calls adjustPrice(hugePrice): price increase has no collateral check, sets a 3-day mint cooldown.
3. After 3 days attacker calls mint(attacker, L): checkCollateral passes because collateral * hugePrice >= minted * 1e18.
4. Attacker keeps L ZCHF; abandoning the dust collateral leaves bad debt covered by the reserve (see DP1-1 for extracting even the collateral).

preconditions.text: no challenge during the 3-day cooldown window (challenges are possible and a challenger would be rewarded via DP1-1 mechanics)

rules_applied: R8:✓(price is cached state used by later mint)
R12:✓(enablers: clone, price raise, cooldown elapsed)
audit_trail.missing_precondition: a challenger/auction during the cooldown that averts or liquidates

title: Zero or dust bids pass minBid and extend a challenge indefinitely at no cost
description: Discovery: Q5.6 (math boundary check, bid = 0 / small). minBid = bid*1005/1000, which is 0 when bid = 0 and equals bid for bid < 200 wei. A bidder can call bid(n, 0, size) every <30 minutes; the 'bump remaining time' branch pushes challenge.end to now + 30 minutes each time, with nothing paid and previous bid not increased. The comment that postponing 'must increase the bid by 0.5% every 30 minutes' does not hold at zero/dust bids. A position owner can keep an undercollateralised position's challenge open forever (blocking liquidation) unless some honest party posts a real bid and escalates.
root_cause: No absolute minimum increment: the 0.5% minimum increase rounds down to 0 for small bids, and a bid equal to the previous one is accepted and still resets the end time.

harm.who: challenger and the protocol (bad debt stays open)
harm.loses_what: the challenger's collateral stays locked and the liquidation of an undercollateralised position is postponed without bound
harm.magnitude: indefinite per challenge; position owner pays only gas

exploit_trace: 1. Owner of an undercollateralised position is challenged.
2. Owner calls bid(n, 0, size) (or 1 wei): tryAvertChallenge fails (bid below price*size), minBid is 0, so the call passes and sets end = now + 30 minutes if end is within 30 minutes.
3. Owner repeats every 29 minutes; the challenge never reaches end() and noChallenge keeps blocking position actions of others/clones.
4. Only a real counter-bid forces the attacker to escalate.

preconditions.text: no honest party posts a non-trivial bid

title: restructureCapTable always indexes addressesToWipe[0], so only the first address is ever wiped
description: Discovery: Q1.2 / CONST-01 (wrong index). The loop variable i is never used; each iteration reads addressesToWipe[0]. A qualified caller who passes several addresses only wipes the first one (the later iterations burn a zero balance). The recapitalisation path described in the NatSpec ('bootstrap the system again owning 100% of all FPS shares') cannot wipe many holders in one call and the extra array entries silently do nothing.

harm.who: qualified FPS holders trying to recapitalise the system
harm.loses_what: ability to wipe passive holders in the restructuring call; they must call the function once per address (and repeat the qualification check)
harm.magnitude: liveness/cost of the last-resort recovery path

exploit_trace: 1. Equity < 1000 ZCHF; a qualified holder calls restructureCapTable(helpers, [A, B, C]).
2. Iterations 0, 1, 2 all burn balanceOf(A); B and C are untouched.
3. Passive holders B and C retain FPS and dilute the recapitalisers.

postconditions.text: unwiped holders keep their FPS shares

postconditions_created: unwiped holders keep their FPS shares

title: Zero-mint clones each take half of the remaining limit of a position (limit stealing / griefing)
description: Discovery: Q5.3 (called repeatedly) / Q3.1. clonePosition is permissionless and charges no fee. With _initialMint = 0, reduceLimitForClone transfers (limit - minted)/2 of the original's limit to the clone. Repeating with minimum collateral halves the original's remaining capacity each time (n clones leave L/2^n); the captured limit sits in clones owned by the attacker, who can use it (see DP1-2) or just starve the original owner and any later cloner.
root_cause: The limit moved to a clone is not tied to the collateral or mint the cloner actually provides, and cloning costs no fee.

harm.who: the original position owner and honest cloners
harm.loses_what: available minting capacity of the position they paid the opening fee for
harm.magnitude: all but L/2^n of the remaining limit after n clones

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker calls clonePosition(P, minCollateral, 0) n times (original not challenged, not in cooldown).
2. Each call moves half of P's remaining limit to the attacker's clone.
3. P's owner can now mint only L/2^n; the attacker owns clones with the captured limit.

preconditions.text: position is past its init period, not expired, not challenged
